skill.name: sharepoint-audit
skill.description: Guide and run a SharePoint audit locally. Collect inputs, confirm PowerShell 7.4+ and Python 3.10+ are available, call PowerShell with certificate auth via wrapper, parse audit.json, and render Markdown/HTML. Use only local shell commands.
skill.summary: Run local SharePoint Online permission audits with certificate authentication and report generation.
skill.author: Aqualia

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally guides local PowerShell and Python execution for SharePoint Online auditing. Several Markdown backtick detections are false positives, but the actual command execution findings are confirmed because they can install modules, process credentials, and access tenant data. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: The workflow runs local PowerShell and Python commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before each command, display the exact command and arguments, and document expected side effects.

remediation.issue: The module installation step can fetch dependencies from the internet.
remediation.suggestion: Pin trusted module versions, document the repository source, and let users review dependencies before installation.

remediation.issue: The audit handles certificate credentials and sensitive permission reports.
remediation.suggestion: Keep secrets in environment variables, avoid logging secret values, and warn users to protect generated reports.

content.value_statement: SharePoint permission audits can be hard to run consistently across one site or many sites. This skill guides a local PowerShell and Python workflow that produces Markdown and HTML audit reports.
actual_capabilities: Collects tenant ID, client ID, PFX path, internal domains, and site targets.
Checks that PowerShell 7.4+, Python 3.10+, and PnP.PowerShell are available locally.
Guides execution of the local module installation and audit agent commands.
Supports a single SharePoint site URL or a CSV-defined batch of sites.
Directs users to generated Markdown and HTML reports under the local runs directory.
Applies safety rules for secret handling and Sites.Selected permission scope.
limitations: Requires the referenced local audit agent files to exist outside the skill file.
Requires valid Microsoft 365 app registration and certificate authentication setup.
Does not independently verify tenant permissions or audit report accuracy.
Generated reports can contain sensitive permission data and need protected storage.

use_cases.title: Audit One SharePoint Site
use_cases.description: Run a focused permission review for a single SharePoint Online site and open the generated report.

use_cases.title: Review Many Sites From CSV
use_cases.description: Use a CSV target list to run repeated audits with the same certificate-based configuration.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Generate local HTML and Markdown reports for access review evidence and follow-up remediation planning.

prompt_templates.title: Start A Single Site Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me audit one SharePoint Online site. Ask for the required tenant, app, certificate, domain, and site details before running anything.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Local Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: Before the audit, confirm that my local environment has the required PowerShell, Python, and PnP.PowerShell prerequisites.

prompt_templates.title: Run A CSV-Based Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through auditing SharePoint sites from a CSV file. Keep Sites.Selected permission at Read unless I explicitly approve Write.

prompt_templates.title: Produce A Secure Audit Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the audit workflow with certificate authentication, avoid printing secrets, and summarize where the sensitive report files are saved.

output_examples.input: Audit the finance SharePoint site using certificate authentication.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for tenant ID, client ID, PFX path, internal domains, site URL, and confirmation that the password environment variable is set.

output_examples.input: Run an audit for a CSV list of sites.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms prerequisites, asks for the CSV path, keeps Sites.Selected permission at Read, and guides local command execution.

output_examples.input: Show me the report after the audit finishes.
output_examples.output: The assistant points to the generated local HTML report and reminds the user that the file contains sensitive permission data.

best_practices: Confirm every local command before execution and review all paths and arguments.
Keep certificate passwords in environment variables and never paste them into chat.
Store generated reports in a protected location with limited access.
anti_patterns: Do not run the audit with broad write permissions unless there is explicit approval.
Do not publish generated reports to shared locations without access controls.
Do not run module installation commands before reviewing the source and dependency trust.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: It guides local command execution. Users should review and confirm commands before they run.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: The workflow requires PowerShell 7.4+, Python 3.10+, and PnP.PowerShell on the local machine.

faq.question: Can it audit multiple SharePoint sites?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions support one site URL or a CSV-defined batch of sites.

faq.question: How are certificate passwords handled?
faq.answer: The skill tells users to keep the PFX password in an environment variable and never echo secrets.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: The skill says to avoid internet access beyond module installation steps.

faq.question: Are the generated reports sensitive?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill warns that generated reports contain sensitive SharePoint permission data.
